items.author: Liam 'Akiba' Wright
items.content:
Quick Take
- CoinGecko announced Solana Foundation backing while pledging that its website, app and API will continue operating as usual.
- Trading remains exploratory, and CoinGecko's growth announcement gives no launch date, execution model, fees or eligibility rules.
- CoinGecko's price methodology requires internal forum approval for changes.
CoinGecko announced Solana Foundation backing on Nov. 17, saying its website, app, and data API will continue operating as usual while the crypto data provider explores trading capabilities.
The company's growth announcement described the relationship as backing without setting out its value, board arrangements, or transaction-specific governance rights. It assures users and businesses that it will keep serving the broader crypto ecosystem as its products evolve.
CoinGecko plans to strengthen its data and API infrastructure and expand coverage of on-chain assets, real-world assets and derivatives. Through that expansion, it aims to serve developers, businesses and financial institutions.
It also plans broader market intelligence and simpler discovery tools, with trading as the third priority. CoinGecko said it is exploring capabilities that connect research and discovery with market participation.
CoinGecko's public methods remain a reference for users
Alongside those plans, CoinGecko pledges to maintain data integrity and keep its methodologies transparent and publicly accessible. Its existing documentation gives data users a concrete reference for how the company says it calculates prices and assesses exchanges.
The published price methodology notes that it collects ticker data across integrated exchanges, excludes anomalous prices, and takes a volume-weighted average of the remaining tickers.
A volume-weighted price gives more weight to higher-volume trades. The resulting figure combines the retained tickers, making the treatment of anomalous prices part of how the displayed aggregate is formed.
The methodology also says changes to price aggregation require prior discussion and approval by a multi-departmental Governance Forum.
CoinGecko's growth announcement does not explain whether the backing gives the Foundation any rights over that process, so continued access to methodology documents is a transparency commitment.
CoinGecko's Trust Score documentation separately points out that exchange-quality assessments are based on liquidity, cybersecurity, regulation, past incidents, and proof of reserves, with scores recalculated weekly.
The measure considers more than an exchange's reported trading volume, with these criteria making exchange ranking a separate assessment from the coin-price calculation.
Users consulting prices and exchange scores are looking at two documented processes with different inputs and purposes.
The documentation also limits how much users can inspect, with CoinGecko saying it will reflect methodology changes in published documentation, while withholding specific thresholds and metric breakdowns to reduce manipulation.
items.title: CoinGecko secures Solana Foundation backing and eyes crypto trading

items.content:
数据：2021年加密独角兽估值普遍缩水50%至70%，行业呈现两极分化

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 18 日，2021—2022 年时期加密市场繁荣期融资的多家独角兽企业，如今在二级市场的股权交易价格较上一轮融资估值折价 50% 至 70%，部分大型项目折价接近 90%。

SecondLane 联合创始人 Omar-Shakeeb Zahir 表示，2021 年的融资轮次如今平均只值当时估值的约 40%。不过，加密行业估值呈现明显分化。支付、稳定币、交易及预测市场领域的头部企业估值持续走高。

Architect Partners 数据显示，自 2025 年 11 月以来，Ripple、Kraken、Kalshi、Polymarket、Crypto.com 和 OKX 等企业参与了 8 轮估值达到 200 亿美元或以上的融资。相比之下，缺乏实际收入的通用型 Layer 1 和 Layer 2、公链中间件及依赖代币激励的消费级应用表现疲软。

今年支付和稳定币企业获得的融资额较 2022 年同期增长 39%，而 NFT、游戏、协议及开发者工具领域融资额下降约 80%。受访投资人士认为，2021 年高估值主要受市场繁荣、低利率及高增长预期推动。随着利率上升、估值倍数收缩，许多企业的实际收入未能支撑此前估值。

Areta 联合创始人 Karl-Martin Ahrend 预计，许多在 2021 年融资的企业将通过并购、资本重组或关闭来解决，2027 年可能成为行业整合之年。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/377905

慢雾：iOS恶意利用链可窃取Keychain、钱包私钥及助记词

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 18 日，慢雾创始人余弦表示，团队对针对 iOS 设备的利用链样本进行溯源分析后，发现攻击者后台面板包含三组利用链：A8 覆盖 iOS 13.0–17.3，B9 覆盖 iOS 18.4–18.7.2，C10 覆盖 iOS 26.0–26.1，可采集 16 类隐私数据。

此外，攻击功能还包括相册原图 OCR 扫描助记词、密码库破解（VaultCrack）以及多链自动洗币（/sweep/execute）。余弦建议，iOS 18 分支设备升级至 18.7.3 及以上，iOS 26 分支设备升级至 26.2 及以上；无法升级至上述系统分支的老旧设备，若系统版本处于 13.0–15.6.x、16.2–16.6.x 或 17.0–17.3.x，建议开启系统「锁定模式」（Lockdown Mode）。该建议同样适用于 iPad 和 Mac 等 Apple 设备。

余弦提醒，利用链一旦通过 Safari 浏览器或 App 等方式成功触发，可能导致设备钥匙串（Keychain）机密数据、备忘录、相册，以及钱包私钥和助记词本地加密文件被采集。

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 18 日，据路透社报道，网站优化平台 Optimizely 确认，其 Experimentation 产品存在漏洞，攻击者利用该漏洞向部分客户项目植入恶意 JavaScript。安全研究员 Scott Helme 表示，这起攻击瞄准了 178 家机构的网站访客，攻击者试图篡改加密货币收款地址、窃取支付卡信息和浏览器 Cookie，并攻击 iOS 设备。

目前尚不清楚有多少用户实际受影响，也没有确认的加密资产损失金额。Optimizely 表示，已修复漏洞并移除受影响项目中的恶意代码。苹果表示，攻击针对的 iOS 漏洞已于去年修复，运行最新软件的用户可免受这些漏洞影响。Zoom 和 Salesforce 已出于预防考虑停用相关脚本；汇丰银行表示，其网站上未运行未经授权的脚本。

items.author: Cointelegraph by Felix Ng
items.content:
Ledger hardware implant saga reaches Dubai’s Virgin Megastore
Two Ledger owners reported losing a combined $604,000 in crypto from hardware wallets they said were purchased at authorized retailer Virgin Megastore in Dubai.
Two Ledger owners have reported cryptocurrency thefts involving hardware wallets they say were purchased from an authorized retailer in Dubai, raising concerns that a hardware wallet tampering campaign had also spread to the UAE.
An X user posting as Rewinsky on Monday said they found their Ledger Flex had been tampered with after reporting the loss of about 1,300 Solana (SOL). Mark Karpelès’ Ledger Implant OSINT registry subsequently confirmed the device as containing a hardware implant.
A second owner, posting as New Babylon Order Worldwide, said Tuesday that 507,000 USDt (USDT) was stolen from their Ledger Stax on Saturday. They said the device was bought new at Virgin Megastore Dubai on Oct. 11, two days after Ledger publicly disclosed an investigation into crypto losses involving devices sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis.
The reports suggest the Ledger device tampering has extended past retailers in just Asia and Europe. Ledger lists Virgin Megastores among its authorized retailers in the United Arab Emirates.
Virgin Megastore lists eight stores in Dubai, including branches at Dubai Mall, Mall of the Emirates and Dubai Hills Mall.
Cointelegraph reached out to Ledger and Virgin Megastore for comment.
Related: Tampered Ledger reported in Singapore a month before news broke: Asia Express
items.title: Ledger hardware implant saga reaches Dubai’s Virgin Megastore

items.author: Liam 'Akiba' Wright
items.content:
Quick Take
- PEAR researchers report 18 successes in 30 physical trials after simulated robot training, compared with none for the base model.
- The final model practiced pickup and block alignment in simulation before testing those task types on different physical hardware.
- Lower-precision decoding speeds describe a separate configuration from the evaluations.
Researchers behind PEAR, a system for training AI models to control robots, reported that a model completed 18 of 30 physical trials after learning its robot skills entirely in simulation.
The preprint submitted Nov. 13 describes robot post-training of Qwen3.8-27B, an open-weight reasoning model with 27 billion parameters. Researchers used reinforcement learning without demonstrations during that stage.
The result offers evidence that simulated practice can teach skills that carry over to different physical hardware. The final model had already practiced the two evaluated task types, pickup and block alignment, in simulation.
What transferred to the real robot
The physical test used a dual-arm YAM robot, which none of the compared models received training on in this study. It included 20 pickup attempts across ten objects and ten alignment attempts across five block layouts, with each object or layout tried twice.
The final model succeeded in 12 pickup attempts and six alignment attempts. A checkpoint trained only on the LIBERO simulation benchmark completed seven of the 30 trials.
The final model had continued training on the corresponding two tasks in RoboDojo using a different robot, according to the paper's physical-trial account.
At each turn, the model reads camera images and the robot's state, reasons in text, and specifies changes to the gripper's pose. Inverse kinematics translates the target pose into joint movements, which a controller executes.
The prompt supplies coordinate frames, gripper orientation, cameras, and task-completion conditions, and the authors acknowledge that performance depends on those descriptions.
All three models used the same high reasoning-effort setting, with trials having a 25-round budget and failing if a single round exceeded 32,000 reasoning tokens. The final model's successful attempts required 7 to 24 rounds.
The authors say reasoning before every move slows tasks. Their separate decoding demonstration reached 747 tokens per second on a GB300 using lower-precision NVFP4 weights and DFlash2, a decoding accelerator.
That suggests about 4.3 seconds to generate an average high-effort reasoning round. The reported evaluations used BF16 weights because quantization reduced accuracy, so the speed demonstration and physical success rate describe different operating conditions.
The public PEAR repository provides training infrastructure and deployment recipes. The result remains an author-reported experiment pending independent replication, and turning it into a broadly useful robot system will require wider task coverage and shorter reasoning delays.
items.title: Researchers train AI in simulation and unlock real robot skills

Serenity解读英伟达财报：需求远超供给，加码内存采购利好美光和三星

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 18 日，Serenity 发文解读英伟达财报，第三财季披露的关键信号是「需求远超供给」。英伟达将 2028 财年营收同比增速预期从约 70% 上调至约 75%。Serenity 认为，供给瓶颈缓解可能是上调预期的原因之一；英伟达称，需求增长和供应增加均为上调提供了支撑。

英伟达提交给美国 SEC 的文件显示，供应承诺从上一季度的 2790 亿美元增至 3900 亿美元，增量主要来自多年期内存采购。Serenity 将此视为美光和三星内存业务的利好。英伟达还与 Kinsus 和三星电机达成新的载板供应协议。

英伟达称，云计算行业积压订单三个月内从 2 万亿美元升至 2.5 万亿美元。部分 Hopper GPU 的多年期租赁续约价格最高达到原价的两倍，B300 租金自推出以来上涨逾 60%。英伟达表示，其服务的大型云厂商和新兴云服务商已充分利用现有英伟达算力。

英伟达第三财季网络业务营收超过 210 亿美元，共封装光学（CPO）交换机已进入量产，Lambda 已宣布投入生产部署。与新兴云服务商合作时，英伟达除获得设备销售收入外，还可在满足特定条件时分享其来自第三方客户的收入。Serenity 认为，这些数据表明，从内存采购到光网络部署，AI 基础设施建设仍在加速，与市场的悲观预期形成反差。

小米MiMo被曝酝酿独立融资，雷军与罗福莉意见不一

动察 Beating AI 快讯，Top 华人科创社消息，小米正讨论是否将 MiMo 大模型业务分拆出来，独立融资。多家知名风投和企业投资机构已初步接触，但小米集团尚未拿出明确方案。

罗福莉及 MiMo 核心研究团队希望将大模型业务独立出来，引入外部融资，但雷军对此仍有不同考虑。双方尚未达成一致，罗福莉已开始接触少数投资人和融资顾问，不排除自行创业的可能。

罗福莉去年 11 月才正式加入小米，今年 9 月便晋升至小米最高职级 22 级。她带队推出的 MiMo-V2.6-Pro，曾登顶 Artificial Analysis 全球开源模型榜单。

小米对 MiMo 也寄予厚望。雷军今年 3 月宣布，未来三年将在 AI 领域投入至少 600 亿元。7 月，小米又调整组织架构，明确由 MiMo 团队为小爱同学提供基础模型能力，服务手机、汽车等终端业务。

如果 MiMo 独立融资，可以引入外部资本，并为研究团队提供单独的股权激励。但小米也需要重新安排对核心 AI 技术的控制，以及 MiMo 与自家手机、汽车和智能家居业务的合作关系。

目前，分拆融资及双方存在分歧的消息尚未获得小米或当事人确认。

分析：比特币流通供应量的一半处于亏损状态，抄底买盘仍未明显回升

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 18 日，据彭博社报道，比特币近期在约 6.4 万美元或更低水平交易，较高位回撤约 50%，但抄底买盘仍未明显回升。Glassnode 数据显示，按上次链上转移时的价格估算，目前约一半流通中的比特币处于账面亏损；9 月下旬比特币收于 8.66 万美元时，这一比例尚不足四分之一。

11 月 15 日发生链上转移的比特币中，按美元计的亏损总额约为盈利总额的 5.6 倍，为 7 月中旬以来最大差距。Glassnode 以比特币上次转移时的价格估算持有成本，但链上转移不一定意味着卖出。同期，短期持有量与长期持有量之比升至 2 月下旬以来最高，长期持有量在约一个月内减少了 112,000 枚比特币。

稳定币供应与比特币 ETF 资金同步承压。截至 11 月 15 日的 30 天内，Glassnode 追踪的稳定币供应量减少约 165 亿美元，主要来自 USDT 和 USDC，两者的余额下降主要集中在交易平台。美国现货比特币 ETF 过去一周也录得逾 8.5 亿美元净流出。彭博社指出，本轮下跌早于周末的强制平仓，美债收益率上升和美元走强也令市场承压。

Anthropic IPO 吸引加密交易者关注，但资金是否从加密资产转向 IPO 尚未得到证实。Hyperliquid 上两份与 Anthropic 估值挂钩的合约，未平仓头寸合计超过 3.34 亿美元。不少参与者此前交易过主流加密货币期货，但现有数据无法表明他们是否卖出了加密资产来为这些头寸筹资。Binance 联合创始人赵长鹏也将资金转向 Anthropic IPO 列为币价下跌的可能原因之一，并强调相关性不等于因果关系。

items.content:
Anthropic IPO风向逆转：估值或升至1.6万亿美元，亚马逊谷歌合持近三成股份

动察 Beating AI 快讯，Anthropic 11 月 17 日再次更新 IPO 招股书，首次明确披露两大科技巨头的持股比例。上市及配套私募完成后，亚马逊将持有 14.7%，谷歌持有 13.7%，合计达到 28.4%。

亚马逊手里还有尚未转换成股票的可转债。如果全部转股，其持股比例理论上可以达到 23.8%。但由于持股上限限制，这部分股份不会在上市时全部转换。

这两家公司同时也是 Anthropic 的重要算力供应商。招股书显示，Anthropic 已承诺在各自合同期内，向亚马逊支付至少 1100 亿美元、向谷歌支付至少 1213 亿美元，用于购买云计算服务。

也就是说，亚马逊和谷歌既能分享 Anthropic 上市后的股权收益，又能通过长期算力合同获得收入。不过，它们持有的是没有普通投票权的股票，Anthropic 创始人仍通过特殊股权安排掌握 50.1% 的投票权。

IPO 定价也出现反转。11 月初还有投资者认为，Anthropic 的估值应该从 1.5 万亿美元降至约 1 万亿美元。如今认购需求已达到发行股份的近七倍。《华尔街日报》最新报道称，Anthropic 可能把发行价提高到每股 80 美元以上，对应估值约 1.5 万亿至 1.6 万亿美元。

不过，11 月 17 日的新文件仍保留每股 70 至 78 美元的发行区间。最终价格预计在 11 月 18 日确定，股票计划于 11 月 19 日在纳斯达克交易。

英伟达第三财季营收按客户总部统计：美国占近63%，未披露东南亚营收占比

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 18 日，据英伟达财报，2027 财年第三季度总营收为 1158.44 亿美元。按直接客户总部所在地统计，美国营收为 728.99 亿美元，占 62.93%；中国台湾为 302.95 亿美元，占 26.15%；中国（含香港）为 110.50 亿美元，占 9.54%；其他地区合计 16 亿美元，占 1.38%。公司未单独披露东南亚营收占比。

新加坡此前曾单列。2026 财年第二季度，按客户账单地址统计，新加坡对应营收为 101.56 亿美元，约占总营收的 22%。英伟达当时披露，在新加坡开票的受出口管制数据中心计算业务收入中，超过 99% 来自美国客户的订单。自 2026 财年第三季度起，公司改按直接客户总部所在地统计，新加坡不再单列。按现行口径，总部在新加坡、马来西亚或印尼的直接客户归入「其他」；若美国总部的直接客户将所购芯片部署在马来西亚，收入仍归入美国。

据 BlockBeats 此前报道，新加坡云服务商 Megaspeed 在马来西亚、印尼等地部署英伟达 GPU，中国客户可远程租用相关算力。彭博社根据两国海关记录估算，从 2023 年成立至 2025 年 11 月，Megaspeed 累计进口至少 46 亿美元的英伟达设备。美国智库 Institute for Progress 估计，到 2026 年底，中国企业可远程使用的海外 AI 算力约相当于 105 万张 H100，相关数据中心约 75% 位于东南亚。但英伟达财报中并未单独披露东南亚营收占比。

美国商务部 11 月 16 日发布新规，收紧经第三国数据中心远程获取先进 AI 算力的限制。英伟达临时 CEO Colette Kress 在电话会上表示，公司仍在评估新规，未量化其对东南亚业务的影响。

美CFTC民主党委员提名人质疑预测市场的公共利益，称希望参与规则制定

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 18 日，美国商品期货交易委员会（CFTC）民主党委员提名人 Matthew Rowland 在参议院农业委员会的确认听证会上表示，联邦法律要求 CFTC 评估部分事件合约的交易是否符合公共利益。监管机构应审慎权衡这类合约的公共利益与经济用途。他表示，若获确认，希望参与预测市场规则的制定。

目前，Kalshi、Polymarket、Coinbase 等平台面临多州提起的诉讼，各州指控相关业务违反州博彩法。部分联邦法院认为，这类业务类似赌场博彩，应受州级监管；平台与 CFTC 则主张，作为受联邦监管的衍生品交易所，相关平台不受州博彩法约束，已有一家联邦法院支持这一立场。CFTC 正通过诉讼维护其监管权限，并已提出针对预测市场的监管规则。

共和党委员提名人 Nathan Anonick 表示，监管权限尚未明确，使预测市场监管变得复杂；若美国最高法院就此作出裁决，他将遵循裁决。民主党参议员 Tina Smith 则强调，争议的核心是《印第安人博彩监管法》以及各州监管体育博彩的权力。

两名提名人均支持补齐 CFTC 法定的五个委员席位，并对按需增聘人员持开放态度。目前，CFTC 仅有主席 Mike Selig 一名在任委员。一名参议员在听证会上指出，尽管监管范围已扩展至预测市场和加密资产，CFTC 的人员规模仍较此前缩减约四分之一。被问及企业与特朗普家族的商业关系是否应影响监管待遇时，两名提名人均表示，执法不应因当事方身份而有所区别。

英伟达已停止向中国交付获许可的Hopper数据中心产品，第三财季相关销售额达24亿美元

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 18 日，据彭博社报道，英伟达已停止向中国交付获美国出口许可的 Hopper 数据中心产品。临时 CEO 兼首席财务官 Colette Kress 在财报电话会上表示，英伟达 2027 财年第三季度在中国销售了价值 24 亿美元的获许可 Hopper 数据中心产品，目前已停止相关出货。她未说明停供原因。英伟达第四财季营收指引未计入来自中国市场的数据中心计算业务收入。

英伟达此前曾争取美国政府允许其向中国销售较先进的 Blackwell 芯片，但未获批准。特朗普政府曾允许英伟达向特定中国客户出口部分 Hopper 架构的 H200 芯片。H200 所属的 Hopper 架构比英伟达目前最先进的 Rubin 架构早两代。黄仁勋上周离任前，一直是英伟达扩大对华芯片销售的主要推动者。

与此同时，美国商务部工业与安全局于 11 月 16 日发布临时最终规则，加强对先进 AI 芯片和服务器远程访问的限制，旨在防止受美国出口限制的企业通过第三国数据中心获取先进算力。英伟达并未将此次停供归因于这项新规。

英伟达董事会于 11 月 17 日宣布成立国家安全与出口管制监督委员会，负责监督公司国家安全政策、出口管制合规及全球贸易风险管理。董事长 Harvey Jones 表示，国家安全因素正在改变英伟达所处的市场，新任 CEO 需要审慎应对。

[pcarolan]: When you typed who is on snl tonight? You used to get 10 pages of clickbait that made you scroll down endlessly for the answer. The best product for most questions is to just give you the answer. That said, the death of discovery is worth mourning. I hope someone solves it but this was dying before ai came along. SEO killed the web, AI killed SEO, and so it goes…

[wraptile]: As someone who did a fair amount of SEO in the past - good.  
Search sucked so bad for the last decade and maybe AI can actually sift through all garbage better than whatever-nothing google's pagerank tried to do. The only danger right now is that people will gate information or stop creating. I think we desperately need cheap easy blogging networks like reddit where people can journal their findings and opinions without restriction because people always want to share, even without being...

[asdfasgasdgasdg]: If Google didn’t put those there, people would be going to other LLMs to get their answers quickly. I don’t know how this ends but I strongly doubt any unilateral effort to withhold llm service by Google changes the medium term outcome.

[nicbou]: My traffic is down over 80%. The information I create is really easy to steal, but it's as expensive as ever to create. I have built a lot of infrastructure to surface that information. I've set up group chats, built relationships, and created tools. Now all that work just feeds the AI that is putting me out of work. By December next year I'll probably have to put the website in maintenance mode and find another job. The problem is that AI also made software development absolut...

[temp3452]: The obvious end to this is ads in ai output. The interesting question is, will google be doing it or will the new (or probably current seo) be writing pages specifically designed to be added to steer ai answers? items.author: Cointelegraph by Felix Ng
items.content:
Nvidia board rejects Huang comeback despite record $116B quarter
Nvidia beat Wall Street’s revenue expectations by 5.6% and issued a stronger-than-expected sales forecast, while its board resisted growing calls for Jensen Huang’s reinstatement.
Nvidia’s board confirmed Tuesday it “does not intend to reinstate” company founder and former CEO Jensen Huang, as the chipmaker reported record quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion, above Wall Street expectations.
Chairman Harvey Jones told investors at the start of Nvidia’s earnings call that the board had unanimously accepted Huang’s resignation. Chief financial officer Colette Kress, who is serving as interim CEO, added later that it was “business as usual” at Nvidia after his departure.
Hours earlier, Huang said on X he would be “honored” to return as CEO, should the board decide his return is in the best interest of shareholders.
The decision pours cold water on a growing campaign to reinstate Huang as CEO. US President Donald Trump and Tesla CEO Elon Musk had both backed his return, while the Wall Street Journal on Monday reported that some employees have discussed holding a demonstration in support of Huang at the company’s Santa Clara campus.
Nvidia revenue more than doubles in Q3
The board’s decision came as Nvidia reported record quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier and 5.6% ahead of the $109.3 billion analysts had expected, according to Visible Alpha consensus data published by S&P Global Market Intelligence.
Data center revenue more than doubled to $107.6 billion, accounting for about 93% of Nvidia’s sales.
Nvidia forecast $130 billion in revenue for the current quarter, above Wall Street’s $125.3 billion estimate and 12% higher than its third-quarter revenue.
Related: ARK sells $85M in Nvidia shares ahead of chipmaker’s Q3 earnings results
Nigel Green, CEO of deVere Group, said the forecast pointed to sustained AI spending.
“This is huge for investors. It shows AI spending is being driven by companies and governments who see the tech as essential, and they’re likely to keep spending big.”
“The AI build-out looks set to run for years, and the gains are likely to spread far beyond the one chipmaker everyone’s watching,” Green added.
Nvidia shares closed 0.4% lower at $155.46 on Tuesday before rising about 4% in after-hours trading following the earnings.
The board also formed a committee to oversee national security and trade compliance. Huang has agreed to appear before Congress on Dec. 1 as lawmakers scrutinize whether Chinese entities gained access to advanced US chips.

items.author: Liam 'Akiba' Wright
items.content:
Quick Take
- Anthropic’s proposed IPO separates 801.35 million new shares from 23.65 million existing-holder shares, with different destinations for the proceeds.
- Staged share releases permit selling, while actual sales, tighter credit and any transmission to Bitcoin liquidity remain conditional.
- The Federal Reserve’s Nov. 13 release shows bank credit rising $58 billion in the later week, without identifying AI-specific lending.
Anthropic’s planned IPO brings a real risk of insider selling, but its share-release schedule does not make a drain on Bitcoin liquidity inevitable.
Arthur Hayes’s Nov. 5 essay puts falling AI share prices at the start of a broader credit squeeze. He argues that insider sales will weaken stocks, make borrowing more expensive or unavailable, curb bank-balance-sheet growth, and reduce the dollar liquidity supporting crypto.
Hayes estimated 83% dilution by June 2027, arguing that roughly $1.245 trillion in new capital would be needed to absorb potential selling at a hypothetical $1.5 trillion IPO valuation.
Anthropic provides a concrete test of the first link, since its offering creates new shares, while subsequent releases also permit existing holders to sell.
Those changes affect supply differently, with different consequences for company fundraising and investors’ ownership.
What changes in the share supply
Anthropic’s Nov. 10 announcement proposes 825 million Class A shares, with 801,351,354 offered by the company and 23,648,646 by existing stockholders, and the AI firm receives no proceeds from the existing holders’ sales.
The preliminary price range is $70 to $78, with an option for underwriters to purchase another 123.75 million shares.
New company shares increase the outstanding share count and raise money for Anthropic. Secondary shares already exist, and selling them transfers ownership and pays the selling holder. A later unlock removes a restriction on selling without issuing another share.
Under the preliminary IPO and concurrent private-placement assumptions, legal Class A and Class N shares together rise from about 11.9 billion to over 13 billion, an increase of approximately 9.66%.
The approximately 15.5 billion Class A-equivalent securities covered by lock-ups are another measure, including Class N shares, awards, and potential note conversions. The pool spans more securities than already-issued Class A stock and differs from freely tradable float.
Awards and convertible instruments can create additional shares when their conditions are met.
The preliminary resale disclosures allow up to approximately 316 million additional shares to become eligible for sale from the first trading day. Further quantities include 299 million at each of 27 and 48 days after the US prospectus date, and 349 million at each of 62 and 76 days.
Non-founder personnel and certain other holders have restrictions ending at the earlier first-quarter results trigger or 180-day endpoint. Co-founders and certain larger holders follow an earlier third-quarter results trigger or 365-day endpoint, with staged early-release exceptions.
Earnings-linked triggers use public results announcements and subsequent trading-day intervals, and representative waivers and other restrictions add further conditions.
Multiplying $1.5 trillion by 83% yields $1.245 trillion, but that's a theoretical value. That interpretation depends on what holders sell, the prices buyers pay, and demand for the stock
The credit evidence has moved
The Federal Reserve’s Nov. 13 H.8 release shows seasonally adjusted bank credit rising from $20.02 trillion on Oct. 28 to $20.08 trillion on Nov. 4, a $58 billion increase.
Published after Hayes’s essay, the release shows aggregate bank credit expanding over the later reported week. Future stress remains possible, and these totals provide no AI-specific lending breakdown or causal evidence about Bitcoin.
Hayes’s warning remains a scenario worth tracking: insider selling, weaker share prices, higher financing costs and reduced lending would support successive links in his argument.
Anthropic’s conditional IPO timetable brings the selling-risk test closer, while the transmission from share supply to Bitcoin liquidity still requires evidence.
items.title: Bitcoin faces a liquidity drain as Anthropic IPO unlocks millions

英伟达电话会：董事会无意请回黄仁勋，2028财年营收增速预期上调至75%

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 18 日，在黄仁勋辞任后的首场财报电话会上，英伟达将 2028 财年营收增速预期从 70% 上调至 75%。临时 CEO 兼首席财务官 Colette Kress 表示，算力需求仍远超供给，新一代 Vera Rubin 产品已贡献约 200 亿美元营收。与此同时，董事长 Harvey Jones 明确表示，董事会无意让黄仁勋复任 CEO，正同时考察内部和外部候选人。

业绩与指引均超预期，Rubin 创公司最快量产纪录。英伟达 2027 财年第三季度营收达 1158 亿美元，高于市场预期的 1093.3 亿美元；第四财季营收指引为 1261 亿至 1339 亿美元，区间下限也高于市场预期的 1252.5 亿美元。财报发布后，英伟达股价盘后一度上涨逾 4%。Kress 解释称，公司上调下一财年增速预期，既考虑了持续增长的需求，也考虑了能够向不同客户提供的新增供给。她表示，Vera Rubin 的量产出货速度创下英伟达历代产品之最。

英伟达将更审慎地为新兴云服务商提供财务担保。Kress 表示，公司正在严格评估各项投资、承诺和担保，未来会更有选择地支持新兴云客户。多数项目的担保并非在开工时即生效，而是以数据中心设施就绪为前提。若施工推迟或遇到障碍，相关担保可能不会生效。

董事会不打算请回黄仁勋，正式 CEO 遴选将「全面而审慎」。Jones 重申，黄仁勋是自愿辞职，董事会不会为加快交接而仓促选定继任者。他指出，新 CEO 需要应对先进芯片业务与国家安全问题交织带来的挑战。董事会未在电话会上回答有关黄仁勋离职经过或正在进行的调查的问题。Kress 则表示，公司运营照常，对客户、合作伙伴和股东的承诺不变。

英伟达第三财季营收1158亿美元超预期，并上调2028财年营收预期，股价盘后涨超4%

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 18 日，据彭博社报道，英伟达发布黄仁勋辞任后的首份财报：2027 财年第三季度营收达 1158 亿美元，同比增长 103%，第四财季营收指引中值为 1300 亿美元，均高于市场预期。公司还将 2028 财年营收增速预期从 70% 上调至 75%。在财报电话会上，英伟达董事长 Harvey Jones 表示，董事会一致接受黄仁勋辞任，无意让他复任 CEO。财报公布后，英伟达股价盘后涨超 4%。

数据中心仍是主要增长来源。截至 10 月 25 日的第三财季，英伟达营收环比增长 20%，超过分析师预期的 1093 亿美元；调整后每股收益为 2.68 美元，高于预期的 2.47 美元。数据中心营收为 1076 亿美元，同比增长 110%，高于预期的 1019 亿美元。其中，超大规模云厂商贡献 601 亿美元，同比增长 71%；AI 云、工业及企业客户贡献 475 亿美元，同比增长 195%。英伟达称，Vera Rubin NVL72 已开始出货，Blackwell Ultra 的销售也继续增长。

第四财季看不到来自中国的数据中心计算收入，毛利率也将下滑。英伟达预计第四财季营收为 1300 亿美元，上下浮动 3%，高于分析师预期的 1253 亿美元；该财季比通常多一周。第三财季，公司向中国出货的数据中心 Hopper 产品金额为 24 亿美元，但管理层表示将不再向中国出货已获出口许可的相关产品，第四财季指引也未计入中国数据中心计算业务收入。公司预计第四财季毛利率为 71% 至 72%，低于第三财季的调整后毛利率 74.9%。临时 CEO 兼 CFO Colette Kress 预计，第四财季将是毛利率低点。

未来支出承诺升至 5180 亿美元，主要增量来自多年期内存采购。这一总额三个月前为 3660 亿美元。其中，供应及产能承诺由 2790 亿美元升至 3900 亿美元，2028 财年对应约 2030 亿美元；云服务协议和尚未开始的 data center 租约合计承诺 1020 亿美元。上述金额是跨多个财年的承诺，并非当季已支付的资本开支。此外，英伟达披露，董事会已于 9 月批准增加 1500 亿美元的股票回购额度，截至第三财季末剩余约 2273 亿美元。

黄仁勋当天早些时候表示，若董事会邀请，他愿意回归。英伟达已启动正式 CEO 遴选，由 Kress 继续担任临时 CEO 并兼任 CFO。Kress 在电话会上表示，公司运营照常，她已与客户、供应商和合作伙伴沟通，并获得各方支持。

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- Microsoft says MAI Code 2 delivers 96% of Claude Opus 5.5's coding performance at 5% of its cost, though the comparison includes promotional pricing.
- Its new cybersecurity model scored 92.3% against GPT-6 Astra's 91.5% on a vulnerability-finding test, according to Microsoft's evaluations.
- MAI Image 2.7 topped an independent image-editing leaderboard, while our quick comparisons favored its realism, creativity and overall output quality.
Microsoft unveiled a new lineup of specialized AI models at its Ignite conference Tuesday, making a direct run at Anthropic and OpenAI in coding, cybersecurity, and image generation.
Instead of trying to build a single chatbot that beats everyone at everything, it is pitching models trained to do particular jobs at substantially lower cost.
The biggest claim involves MAI Code 2, which Microsoft says delivers 96% of Claude Opus 5.5's performance on common enterprise coding tasks for just 5% of the cost. It also claims 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol's performance at 40% of the price.
OpenAI also released GPT-6.2 on Tuesday, so Microsoft’s Sol comparison already concerns an older generation.
Those figures average results from four evaluations focused on practical software development, including fixing code and completing multi-file changes. Microsoft ran three of the tests on its own evaluation platform, used outside results for the fourth, and calculated MAI Code 2's costs using a 50% promotional discount.
A lighter Code 2 Flash model targets routine fixes and quick edits, with Microsoft claiming performance comparable to Claude Haiku 5.5 at 20% of the price, so extremely cheap without sacrificing quality. Both coding models are already in GitHub Copilot, putting Microsoft's in-house technology directly into a product that has relied heavily on outside AI suppliers.
Security is another target. Microsoft says MAI Cyber 2 Flash succeeded on 92.3% of CyberGym-E2E's evaluated vulnerability-discovery tasks, compared with 91.5% for GPT-6 Astra, at less than 2% of the cost per task. CyberGym-E2E scores the percentage of software-security investigations an AI completes successfully; Microsoft excluded 92 of 905 tasks after identifying overlap between their source material and its training data.
The company has not yet published a direct comparison against OpenAI's restricted GPT-6 Cyber model. Its security system will begin replacing an older MAI model for eligible MDASH customers in mid-December, building on the vulnerability-scanning approach Decrypt previously covered.
In AI, David can also beat Goliath
Can a small model beat a big one? Definitely—in specific cases.
A general-purpose model has to learn to write poetry, explain physics, debug software and answer questions about almost anything. A model tuned for coding or cyber defense can spend more of its training and computational budget on the patterns that matter for that job, rather than carrying the same breadth of knowledge into every request.
That doesn't make smaller models universally smarter. It can make them faster and more economical when the task is well defined, particularly in a business where the same work runs thousands of times a day.
A security scanner analyzing every new code change does not need an expensive frontier model to explain the history of the Roman Empire. If a model can dedicate its full power to generate Python code, it will make more sense to pay for its API calls instead of using a super powerful generalistic model.
Specialization can also improve the whole system around the model: the tools it calls, the checks that verify its answers and the data used to refine it. OpenAI has taken a related approach with its Mini and Nano models, letting cheaper workers handle routine tasks while larger systems tackle the exceptions.
However, there are trade-offs. Microsoft's own documentation says Code 2 is not yet optimized for fundamental scientific research or very long-running autonomous assignments. And Anthropic competes in the cheaper end of the market with Haiku, not just its premium Opus models, so Microsoft is entering a race its rivals already understand.
MAI Image is the more convincing demonstration
Microsoft's MAI Image 2.7 may offer the clearest evidence that its strategy is working. In our quick side-by-side tests, its images beat GPT Image and Google's Nano Banana on realism, creativity, and overall quality.
These were just first impressions based on a few generations, but they broadly track its strong showing in independent rankings.
On Artificial Analysis's image-editing test, which asks people to choose between anonymously generated edits and turns those preferences into an Elo rating, MAI Image 2.7 currently leads with 1,215 points against GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst's 1,211.
The four-point gap is small enough that their reported uncertainty ranges overlap; the separate text-to-image generation ranking, scored using the same preference-based method, puts Microsoft in fourth place.
The pricing is harder to ignore. Microsoft quotes about $35 per 1,000 images for MAI Image 2.7 and $10 for its Flash version, versus roughly $211 for GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst at maximum quality in Artificial Analysis's comparison. Google's Nano Banana 2.1 is about $34 per 1,000 there, while Nano Banana Pro is about $134; actual bills depend on the provider, resolution and settings.
Our earlier testing of MAI Image 2 found excellent realism but frustrating limits on editing and output formats. The newer release adds interactive editing through Microsoft's Canvas workspace, transparent backgrounds and broader access through Foundry, although image quality and a usable product are still two different things. That said the model is quite censored too.
Microsoft is also offering selected business customers the ability to customize and run its models' licensed weights inside Azure, reducing reliance on outside vendors without making the technology open source. For the next test of its specialist strategy, Code 2 is already available in GitHub Copilot, and the Cyber 2 Flash rollout is scheduled to start in mid-December.

items.content:
Quick Take
- Three addresses held virtually all 52.91 million USDf tokens on XRPL EVM in a Nov. 17 snapshot.
- DefiLlama tracked $22,415 in DeFi TVL and $0.09 in 24-hour chain fees, separate from bridged stablecoin inventory.
- XRP is required for gas, but concentrated USDf balances do not establish usable liquidity or sustained new XRP buying.
Three addresses hold virtually all the dollar-pegged USDf token supply on XRP Ledger (XRPL) EVM, an XRP-powered smart contract sidechain, according to a Nov. 17 explorer snapshot.
The contract contains 52.9 million tokens, while DefiLlama values the chain's tracked bridged stablecoin inventory at about $52.7 million.
DefiLlama reports $22,415 in total value locked (TLV) in tracked DeFi protocols and just $0.09 in chain fees over 24 hours. Tokens are present, but measured application activity and fee expenditure remain small.
XRPL EVM is a separate blockchain from the native XRP Ledger. Its official documentation describes a sovereign layer-1 that runs Ethereum-compatible smart contracts and uses XRP for transaction fees.
That gives XRP a direct role in operating the chain, without making every dollar bridged there a dollar spent buying XRP.
Where the USDf inventory sits
On Nov. 17, the USDf contract metadata showed a supply of 52,906,708 tokens. The holder list showed four balances: 40 million USDf in the largest, about 7 million in the second, and 5.9 million in the third.
Those positions represent about 75.6%, 13.25%, and 11.15% of supply, respectively. The fourth address, labeled SquidMulticall, held one smallest unit, or 0.000000000000000001 USDf.
The three large addresses have no names or public tags in that response, so they cannot safely be described as three independent investors, customers, or beneficial owners.
Falcon Finance reported the bridge route in a recap published July 14, 2025, and said USDf was among the assets included in $100 million bridged to XRPL EVM through Axelar.
DefiLlama's Nov. 17 stablecoin API entry records 52,906,708 circulating dollar-pegged units and a dollar valuation of $52,674,373.43, implying about $0.9956 per unit.
Its separate chain dashboard displayed $52.6 million in stablecoin market capitalization, with USDf accounting for all tracked stablecoins.
The $22,415 DeFi total measures another category. Under DefiLlama's methodology, chain TVL sums assets deposited in tracked protocols, while bridge TVL is excluded from chain totals. The difference between inventory and TVL cannot be read as missing money, or used to establish that every token outside tracked protocols is idle.
Tokens can be present without the data demonstrating deep trading liquidity, broad participation, or sustained borrowing and lending. Dollar TVL also changes with token prices, making token balances and application activity necessary companions to the valuation.
What the activity means for XRP
The same DefiLlama dashboard reported zero in tracked decentralized-exchange volume over 24 hours and $5.37 over seven days, with its reported chain fees at $0.09 over 24 hours.
The chain explorer series counted 1,365 on Nov. 16, the latest full calendar day, following 1,004 on Nov. 15 and 1,020 on Nov. 14.
Paying fees uses XRP, but the stock of USDf does not establish fresh XRP purchases, the size of users' XRP holdings, or persistent demand to replenish them.
Broader balance distribution, usable trading depth, and repeated application transactions would strengthen the case for functioning liquidity.
Repeated XRP fee expenditure would demonstrate continued gas use, while evidence of fresh purchases would be needed to establish new buying demand.
items.title: Three wallets hoard $52.7M on XRP’s sidechain, and nobody is trading it

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- Nvidia's board explicitly ruled out reinstating Jensen Huang during Tuesday's earnings call.
- Heidrick & Struggles will lead the search for a permanent CEO, while Colette Kress remains interim chief.
- A new board committee will oversee national security and compliance with U.S. chip export restrictions.
Traders, fanboys, investors and believers. It’s time to stop coping.
Nvidia's board has publicly shut down hopes of Jensen Huang returning as CEO, delivering its strongest statement yet against reinstating the company's co-founder following his resignation last week.
"The Nvidia board does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," board chair Harvey Jones said during Tuesday's earnings call.
Jones said the board unanimously accepted Huang's resignation and would not answer questions about the circumstances surrounding his departure or the ongoing independent investigation.
The company has hired executive recruitment firm Heidrick & Struggles to find a permanent replacement. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress, who took over as interim CEO, received the board's full backing.
"We have every confidence in Colette's leadership, integrity and ability to deliver as interim CEO," Jones said.
The declaration comes just hours after Huang publicly offered to return if directors believed his reinstatement would benefit shareholders and employees. Earlier today, before Huang’s public statement, sources told CNBC the board was not considering bringing Huang back.
Huang resigned after revelations about extramarital relationships, including one involving a businesswoman whose alleged Chinese intelligence connections have attracted scrutiny from U.S. authorities. An independent investigation is examining his conduct and potential national security implications.
His departure prompted an unusual campaign for reinstatement, with President Donald Trump and Elon Musk among those publicly supporting his return.
China scrutiny intensifies
Jones also defended Nvidia's newly established National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee, saying it would improve engagement with U.S. officials as Washington investigates how restricted AI chips have reached China.
The committee, chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson, will oversee compliance programs and receive reports directly from Nvidia's national security and trade compliance teams.
Nvidia reported $2.5 billion in quarterly revenue from sales to Chinese business units under the Trump administration's limited export permissions.
Those arrangements face renewed uncertainty following reports that billions of dollars in restricted Nvidia hardware reached mainland China through overseas intermediaries.
The leadership confrontation overshadowed otherwise impressive quarterly results. Nvidia reported $115.8 billion in revenue, up 103% year over year, with data center sales reaching $107.6 billion.
The company forecast $130 billion in revenue for its fourth fiscal quarter, while assuming no data center computing revenue from China.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Nate Kostar
items.content:
CFTC halts some Kalshi Trump mention markets over manipulation concerns
The CFTC stayed Kalshi’s Trump-related mention markets after raising concerns about manipulation risks, giving the platform until Dec. 11 to defend its contracts.
The US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has ordered a temporary halt to certain Kalshi prediction markets allowing traders to bet on words or phrases US President Donald Trump might say, citing concerns about potential manipulation.
In a Nov. 13 order, the CFTC targeted Kalshi’s “What nicknames will Trump say before 2027?” market and its TRUMPSAY contract series. The regulator said Kalshi had listed the nickname market after a Sept. 22 staff advisory warning of manipulation risks without updating its certification to address those concerns.
The CFTC confirmed to Cointelegraph that it had stayed the listing of certain Kalshi mention markets pending further proceedings. Kalshi has until Dec. 11 to respond, and the regulator has not made a final determination on whether the contracts comply with federal law.
“We disagree with this decision,” Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour told Axios on Tuesday. He argued that markets predicting Trump’s words have economic value because the president’s remarks can move financial markets.
In its September advisory, CFTC staff warned that people whose actions determine a contract’s outcome, or those close to them, could influence the result or exploit advance knowledge of it.
Kalshi had previously stopped listing numerous other mention markets at the regulator’s request, including all sports-related mention contracts, Reuters reported, citing a person familiar with the matter.
Related: Kalshi ends Donald Trump Jr. advisory role over Polymarket investment: Reuters
Teleprompter case highlights insider risks
The regulatory action follows an earlier insider-trading case involving Gabriel Perez, a former White House teleprompter operator who used advance knowledge of President Trump’s speeches to profit from Kalshi contracts, according to the CFTC.
In July, Cointelegraph reported that Kalshi’s surveillance system had flagged Perez’s trades and referred them to the CFTC. The regulator’s subsequent Aug. 28 enforcement order found that Perez generally had access to Trump’s prepared speeches about an hour before delivery and used the information to bet on whether specific words would be spoken. He profited on 39 of 43 contracts across 14 mention markets and, on one occasion, changed his position after Trump skipped or deviated from part of a prepared speech.
In August, the CFTC ordered Perez to return $107,539 in profits and pay a $65,000 civil penalty for trading on nonpublic information. Perez settled without admitting the agency’s findings.

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- Nvidia reported $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue, up 103% from a year earlier, while adjusted earnings reached $2.68 per share.
- Shares rose roughly 2% after hours as the company forecast $130 billion in fourth-quarter revenue, above analysts' expectations.
- Interim CEO Colette Kress faces her first earnings call without Jensen Huang, while Nvidia's daily chart still shows strong selling pressure despite oversold conditions.
Nvidia shares climbed roughly 2% in after-hours trading Tuesday after the AI chipmaker delivered another record quarter, beating Wall Street expectations on revenue and earnings while forecasting stronger-than-expected sales for the current period.
The results offered some relief to investors after a brutal selloff that wiped hundreds of billions of dollars from Nvidia's market value following the resignation of co-founder Jensen Huang.
According to Nvidia's earnings release, revenue reached $115.8 billion for the fiscal third quarter ended October 25, up 103% from a year earlier and comfortably above analysts' expectations of approximately $109.1 billion.
Adjusted earnings per share came in at $2.68, beating the roughly $2.47 consensus estimate. Net income under generally accepted accounting principles reached $65.3 billion, more than double the $31.9 billion reported a year earlier.
Nvidia's data center division generated $107.6 billion in revenue, up 110% year over year and accounting for approximately 93% of total sales. The company also confirmed that its Vera Rubin NVL72 computing platform has begun shipping, extending the hardware roadmap that helped make Nvidia the dominant supplier of AI processors.
The company expects fourth-quarter revenue of $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, compared with Wall Street estimates of approximately $125.3 billion, per Reuters. That forecast includes an additional week in the reporting period and assumes no data center computing revenue from China.
Nvidia's first earnings without Jensen Huang
Tuesday's report marks Nvidia's first financial results since Huang resigned November 12, ending his 33-year tenure following revelations of extramarital affairs involving company employees and a businesswoman suspected by U.S. intelligence officials of having ties to China. Those intelligence allegations remain unproven, and an independent investigation is ongoing.
To add more drama to the story, the Securities and Exchange Commission opened a civil investigation into whether Nvidia violated investor-disclosure laws.
Colette Kress, Nvidia's longtime chief financial officer and interim CEO, sought to reassure investors about the company's future. "Our momentum is real," she said in the earnings announcement, adding that the Vera Rubin rollout was off to a strong start and the product roadmap remained on track.
Huang said Tuesday that he would be honored to return as CEO if the board believed it was in Nvidia's best interests. His statement followed public support from Elon Musk and President Donald Trump, although the board is not considering reinstatement and continues searching for a permanent replacement.
Can Nvidia's stock recover?
Nvidia's fundamentals look considerably better than its stock chart. Despite Tuesday's rebound, shares remain roughly 35% below their October peak near $240, and the technical indicators suggest sellers still control the broader trend.
The daily chart shows immediate support around $150, close to the $148.80 low reached during last week's selloff. A decisive break below that area could expose further downside, while a sustained recovery would first need to reclaim resistance around $164.40 to $165.60.
That former support area has become resistance following the breakdown, as Decrypt's earlier technical analysis identified. Above it, the chart shows additional hurdles near $176 and between $184 and $189, making a return to the previous trading range far from automatic.
The Relative Strength Index, or RSI, is around 22.5 on the supplied daily chart, well below the conventional oversold threshold of 30. That makes a short-term rebound plausible, but oversold readings are not proof that a bottom has formed.
The Average Directional Index, or ADX, sits near 45.4, indicating a strong prevailing trend, with directional signals favoring sellers. The faster exponential moving average remains above the slower one, a positive longer-term configuration that has not prevented the recent collapse.
Tuesday's earnings beat gives bulls a potential catalyst, but the after-hours bounce has yet to reclaim the chart's first major resistance around $164.40. Kress is scheduled to lead the company's 5 p.m. Eastern earnings call, the first without Huang, as investors look for answers about Nvidia's leadership and its next phase of growth.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Jona Jaupi
items.content:
Maple Finance CEO targets up to $15B in assets by the end of 2027
Sidney Powell aims to reach $15 billion in assets under management by the end of 2027 as the firm looks to expand into tokenized lending and traditional finance.
Onchain asset manager Maple Finance is aiming to grow its assets under management (AUM) to between $10 billion and $15 billion by the end of 2027 as it looks to attract more traditional financial (TradFi) firms, according to CEO Sidney Powell.
In an exclusive interview with Cointelegraph on Monday, Powell said the company is also targeting a loan book of around $4.5 billion to $5 billion.
The plans come as Maple looks to grow beyond lending backed primarily by cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin (BTC) and attract more traditional financial firms, with Powell expecting tokenized assets and stablecoins to play a major role in the company’s growth.
Maple reported $4.7 billion in AUM at the end of the third quarter, up 18% from a year earlier. However, Maple’s dashboard showed around $3.9 billion in AUM on Tuesday.
Outstanding loans rose 12% from a year earlier to $1.7 billion, while quarterly revenue increased 5% to $4.4 million, bringing annualized revenue to $17.6 million. Still, outstanding loans fell 9% from the previous quarter, while quarterly revenue remained flat.
Tokenized assets are digital versions of traditional assets, such as stocks and bonds, that can be held and traded on a blockchain. Separately, stablecoins are digital tokens designed to maintain a stable value relative to a reference asset, most commonly a currency such as the US dollar.
The market for tokenized real-world assets has grown significantly over the past year, with their value on public blockchains reaching about $39.9 billion as of Nov. 11, up 52% year-over-year, according to RWA.xyz. The value of tokenized stocks alone rose from about $678 million in January to nearly $3.9 billion in November.
Maple assets under management. Source: Maple Finance
Maple looks to TradFi for its next stage of growth
Powell expects tokenized stocks to grow fivefold to tenfold in 2027, which could allow Maple to offer loans backed by tokenized shares rather than relying mainly on cryptocurrency collateral.
“I think tokenized equities are going to be really big,” he said. “You’ll start to see more tokenized equity lending.”
Under this model, borrowers could use tokenized stocks as collateral to obtain loans without having to sell their investments, similar to how Bitcoin-backed lending works today.
“Ultimately, that’s really positive for the space because it gives you tokenized assets to lend against that are not correlated with Bitcoin,” Powell said. Bitcoin is the largest cryptocurrency with a market capitalization of over $1.28 trillion as of Nov. 17.
Maple is also discussing credit facilities through which banks would finance its Bitcoin-backed lending, Powell said.
“At the moment, we’re looking at a first deal where we’re speaking with banks about warehouse facilities for the Bitcoin-backed lending, so they would be a funder to us,” Powell said.
Maple already provides financing for a warehouse facility supporting Kraken’s crypto-backed lending program, which was announced in June. The proposed bank arrangements would instead bring funding into Maple’s lending business.
Powell added that Maple could pursue separate deals with US banks and lenders involving loans originated by TradFi institutions and subsequently brought onto blockchain networks. “I think that’s going to be a big market for 2027,” he said.
Maple outlined plans in September to lend against portfolios of asset-backed and mortgage-backed securities and finance loans originated by fintech companies. It said at the time that each new strategy would initially be capped at 5% of its overall deposit base.
Another priority is expanding partnerships with financial technology companies and digital banks that want to offer customers ways to earn interest on their stablecoin holdings. Powell said Maple is already in discussions with several large firms about potential products, with announcements possible in the first quarter of 2027.
“My view is that’s the kind of path Maple has to go down in order to grow, and we have to focus more on these larger institutional allocators,” Powell said. “That’s ultimately where most of the balance sheet is in traditional finance.”
That approach to expansion is also at the center of the leadership disagreement, according to Powell.
Related: Arch Lending eyes tokenized stocks as next collateral market
Leadership shakeup comes amid expansion plans
Maple’s growth plans come amid a leadership shakeup after co-founder and executive chairman Joe Flanagan and chief operating officer Ryan O’Shea announced plans last week to leave over disagreements about the company’s future direction.
Flanagan said his differences with Powell involved strategy and leadership, while O’Shea said he had reached a different view on the direction Maple should take.
Powell said the differences centered on how best to expand the business, particularly as TradFi institutions become more involved in crypto lending.
“We had a difference of opinion on the best way to scale things,” he told Cointelegraph. “This year, I think, more than ever, we started to see that real convergence with traditional finance, fintechs and neobanks. And my view is that that is kind of the right path for us to scale.”
The planned departures prompted questions from Maple’s investors, partners and clients, some of whom contacted Powell seeking clarification. Powell said the departures were unrelated to problems with Maple’s loan book or the health of the business.
“The important thing is conveying to them and reassuring them that this wasn’t to do with any issues in Maple’s loan book or any issues with the business,” Powell said. “It is just a difference on what is the best pathway to scale Maple from here.”
Maple Finance’s native token, SYRUP is currently trading at $0.103 as of 6:50 pm UTC on Tuesday, with a market capitalization of $123 million, according to CoinMarketCap. The token is down about 46% over the past 30 days and 74% over the past year.

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, promising stronger professional work at lower task costs.
- Independent tests rank Astra second behind Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2, with no improvement in coding-agent performance.
- Astra is OpenAI's first publicly released model rated High for AI self-improvement, bringing stricter oversight.
OpenAI launched GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol on Tuesday, updating its flagship and everyday AI models with better professional output, cheaper processing and stronger abilities to operate software on their own.
Astra targets demanding projects such as financial spreadsheets, legal research and interactive 3D design. Sol handles everyday work at a lower price, an increasingly important distinction as AI agents spend hours completing tasks instead of answering a single prompt.
When early users tested Astra in September, they built virtual cities and games, but complained its writing and creative capabilities had slipped. The new release claims to address that less glamorous problem, producing documents that look like something a professional would actually send.
Astra costs $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens through OpenAI's API, down 20% from the original model. Sol retains its $2 and $10 rates. Tokens are the chunks of text models process and generate, so fewer tokens can mean a smaller bill even when the listed rates stay the same.
OpenAI says Astra follows slide templates and spreadsheet conventions better, with less boilerplate and more consistent layouts. Those are company claims, not guarantees for every assignment.
Close to the top, cheaper to run
Independent testing by Artificial Analysis puts Astra at 62 on its Intelligence Index, just a bit behind Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 at 65. The index combines nine tests of reasoning, scientific work, coding and knowledge into a score out of 100.
That's five points above GPT-6 Astra, which arrived in September with a much higher price and major cybersecurity restrictions. Sol scores 57, matching the original Astra's performance at roughly 15% of its cost per evaluated task.
Those mixed results follow Anthropic's Fable 5.2 launch last week, when developers demonstrated ambitious games and applications but reported eye-watering costs for long-running projects. Alibaba entered the conversation Monday with Qwen 4 Max, a Chinese flagship that charges $1.50 per million input tokens and $4.50 per million output tokens, although it trails the American leaders in global agent rankings.
Smarter models, tighter controls
OpenAI says Astra is its first externally released model to reach the High threshold for AI self-improvement, a safety classification measuring how much it can accelerate AI research. The company estimates its productivity impact as comparable to giving each researcher an additional capable engineering assistant, relative to 2024.
Both new models also meet OpenAI's Critical cybersecurity threshold. The company says it strengthened monitoring and built a system called Control Room to halt suspicious model activity; testing nevertheless found the models sometimes failed to disclose missing files or unavailable tools that blocked their work.
OpenAI says the models are available through ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users, and through the API for developers, but our GPT Plus subscription still doesn’t show those models, so this may be a slow rollout.
OpenAI has not yet added GPT-6.2 to its Daybreak program for vetted cybersecurity researchers.

items.author: Andjela Radmilac
items.content:
Quick Take
- MSCI will remove Strategy from its USA Index after Nov. 30.
- Three BlackRock ETFs hold 123,056 Strategy shares worth $13.7 million.
- How many shares those funds will actually sell remains unknown.
When you buy an index fund, you're paying a manager to follow a particular group of stocks. MSCI creates these indexes and sets their membership rules, while companies such as BlackRock manage the funds that follow them.
MSCI is removing Strategy from several of its indexes after Nov. 30. Funds following those indexes will then be trying to match the performance of a group that no longer includes Michael Saylor's Bitcoin-buying company.
It's easy to see why investors expect selling: a fund that bought Strategy to follow an index loses that reason to own it when the stock drops out. But two BlackRock funds tracking the same MSCI index show why we can't simply add up all their investments and treat the total as a sell order.
One owns thousands of Strategy shares, while the other uses contracts with financial institutions to get the index's performance. Both managers have to account for the same change, but they don't have to do it through the same trades.
Their fund documents and published holdings let us follow part of that adjustment, including 123,056 Strategy shares reported by three BlackRock funds on Nov. 13, without pretending we know exactly how much stock will be sold at the end of the month.
Buying the stocks or buying their performance?
MSCI's indexes put together stocks that meet a set of rules, such as company size and location, and assign each a share of the index's overall value.
A stock with a larger weight has more influence over how the index performs. The index serves as a benchmark, or performance target, for funds that follow it.
The MSCI USA Index includes large and midsize US companies, and Strategy's Class A shares are scheduled to leave it at the close of trading on Nov. 30, with the change taking effect Dec. 1. MSCI applied new eligibility rules for companies it classifies as non-operating, and Strategy was among the stocks selected for removal.
Other changes to specialized versions of MSCI's indexes are due to be announced on Nov. 18.
BlackRock's iShares MSCI USA ETF (MLRG) follows that US index and trades under the symbol MLRG. As an exchange-traded fund, investors buy and sell shares on a stock exchange while the manager handles the investments inside. Its published holdings included 5,227 Strategy shares on Nov. 13, worth about $583,000.
MLRG uses what's called representative sampling: the manager chooses a collection of investments designed to behave like the index without promising to own every stock on the list at every moment.
Its prospectus, the document setting out how the fund invests, says it intends to keep all or substantially all its assets in index stocks at roughly their index weights. It also allows some investments outside the index when they help the fund follow its performance, including around expected membership changes.
That gives the manager some flexibility while keeping the fund tied to its performance target. Strategy's departure is a reason to adjust the portfolio, but the documents don't require all 5,227 shares reported on Nov. 13 to be sold together at the Nov. 30 close.
BlackRock has another fund that follows the very same index: the iShares MSCI USA Swap UCITS ETF, traded in Europe under symbols including MUSD. This one owns a separate collection of developed-market stocks and uses contracts called total return swaps.
Under its investor document, the fund exchanges that stock portfolio's performance with financial institutions for the performance of the MSCI USA Index.
You're still buying a fund designed to follow MSCI USA, but the contracts provide that connection rather than a portfolio that reproduces the index stock for stock. When Strategy leaves, it stops contributing to the index performance those contracts are meant to deliver.
That doesn't tell us whether MUSD owns Strategy in its separate stock portfolio or whether it will sell any shares.
The counterparties of those contracts may also adjust their own investments to manage the risk they've taken on. Their trades aren't disclosed in these fund documents, so multiplying MUSD's assets by Strategy's index weight wouldn't tell us how many shares the fund has to sell.
The Strategy shares we can actually count
BlackRock's iShares MSCI World ETF (URTH) follows companies across developed markets, including the US, and reported 29,345 Strategy shares, worth about $3.3 million, on Nov. 13.
Its iShares MSCI ACWI ETF follows companies in both developed and emerging markets and reported 88,484 shares, worth about $9.9 million, on the same date. These broader indexes include the US segment, so Strategy's removal from MSCI USA also affects them.
Together with MLRG, those funds held 123,056 Strategy shares valued at $13.74 million. We're looking at three identified portfolios on a particular day, rather than every fund affected by MSCI's decision.
Both URTH and ACWI also use representative sampling, so their managers have some flexibility in how they match their indexes.
Reported holdings on Nov. 13, 2026. This is a selected sample of iShares funds, not every MSCI-linked fund or a forecast of shares to be sold.
The iShares ESG Advanced MSCI USA ETF (USXF) follows a version of MSCI USA that applies additional screening rules to companies. It reported 16,144 Strategy shares on Nov. 13, but as of Nov. 17, the standard-index announcement doesn't establish what will happen in this particular version.
MSCI's announcement for those specialized indexes is still due Nov. 18, so USXF isn't included in the three-fund subtotal.
| Fund | Benchmark and method | Strategy shares reported Nov. 13 | What changes with the index exit | 
|---|---|---|---|
| MLRG · iShares MSCI USA ETF | MSCI USA; holds stocks using representative sampling | 5,227 | Strategy leaves its benchmark after Nov. 30. The prospectus doesn't specify an exact sale order or execution date. | 
| URTH · iShares MSCI World ETF | MSCI World; holds stocks using representative sampling | 29,345 | The US deletion affects the broader developed-market benchmark. Reported holdings don't establish how the fund will dispose of shares. | 
| ACWI · iShares MSCI ACWI ETF | MSCI ACWI; holds stocks using representative sampling | 88,484 | The US deletion affects the broader global benchmark. Reported holdings don't establish how the fund will dispose of shares. | 
| USXF · iShares ESG Advanced MSCI USA ETF | Screened MSCI USA benchmark | 16,144 | As of Nov. 17, treatment of its specific benchmark remains pending the Nov. 18 derived-index announcement. | 
| MUSD · iShares MSCI USA Swap UCITS ETF | MSCI USA; obtains index returns through swaps alongside a separate stock portfolio | Not established in this review | The index return delivered through the swaps changes. The documents don't establish sales from its separate portfolio or its counterparties' hedges. | 
Investors holding Strategy through a fund tied to another index don't automatically face the same change. For example, Invesco QQQ follows the Nasdaq-100, which has its own provider and membership rules.
Managers paid to choose stocks themselves can also keep assessing Strategy on their own terms, as can anyone who owns its shares directly.
Approximate Strategy holdings per $10,000 of fund assets on Nov. 13, 2026: reported portfolio weight divided by 100, then multiplied by $10,000. Inputs are rounded by iShares. These amounts are not forecasts of losses or required sales. USXF follows a screened index; its specific deletion treatment remains pending the Nov. 18 announcement as of Nov. 17.
In its response to MSCI's consultation, Strategy said that funds following the provider's global investable indexes held about 13 million of its shares, equivalent to 3.1% of basic shares outstanding.
That's a much broader estimate than the three-fund sample here, but the published statement doesn't identify the individual funds or give a current observation date for their holdings.
Following the change without inventing the trades
After the index changes, daily holdings files will let us compare what these funds owned before and afterward. Those files can show that a portfolio has fewer Strategy shares, but they won't necessarily show how the shares left it or why.
ETFs can grow or shrink as investors put money in or take it out. When a fund grows, its Strategy holding could increase simply because it needs more of the stocks it already owns.
Comparing the number of Strategy shares with the number of the fund's own shares helps separate fund growth from changes in how much of its portfolio it assigns to Strategy.
When an ETF shrinks, some stocks can leave through the process used to redeem its shares. Financial institutions can hand fund shares back to the ETF and receive underlying securities in return.
Strategy stock could leave the ETF without the fund itself selling it on an exchange, and the institution receiving that stock would then decide what to do with it. The next holdings file would record the smaller position without telling us about those later decisions.
MUSD adds another limit to what we can observe because its contracts deliver the index performance. Its counterparties could adjust their investments as Strategy leaves, but following only the fund's stock holdings wouldn't capture those decisions.
Even when we can see holdings change, comparing two dates won't show how much of Strategy's share-price movement was driven by MSCI, especially when investors can trade ahead of the announced change.
Strategy will still lose a place in the performance target these funds are paid to follow.
That could weaken demand for its stock and make raising money less attractive for a company that sells securities to finance Bitcoin purchases, although the index removal doesn't require Strategy to sell any Bitcoin itself.

items.author: Decrypt Staff
items.content:
In brief
- The World Bank Group said it will explore using Circle’s USDC and blockchain-based payment rails, alongside Citi’s banking connections, to make its global development-funds disbursement faster, cheaper and more transparent than correspondent banking.
- The effort builds on FundsChain, its blockchain platform already tracking disbursements across 350-plus projects in 96 countries.
- It’s a major institutional validator for stablecoins, fitting a Wall Street-onchain wave, from a $270 million bank stablecoin venture to Deutsche Bank’s crypto custody launch.
The World Bank is turning to stablecoins to modernize how it moves development money, announcing Tuesday it will explore using Circle’s USDC and blockchain-based payment rails to speed up and cut the cost of disbursing funds around the world.
The institution said it will work with Citi and Circle to test how dollar-denominated, regulated stablecoins could operate alongside or improve its existing funds-distribution system, which runs on correspondent banking, the slow and costly network of intermediary banks that routes international payments.
Under the arrangement, Citi would supply its connections to established banking rails while Circle provides the infrastructure to mint and settle funds in USDC.
The logic is that even small efficiency gains, applied across the vast sums the World Bank moves, could free up meaningful resources for development. “This initiative is about exploring ways to make the financial plumbing of development work better for the people who need it most,” said World Bank Group President Ajay Banga, arguing that faster, cheaper money movement means “a health clinic gets built on time, a farmer gets paid before the harvest season ends.”
The effort builds on FundsChain, a World Bank blockchain platform designed to make fund disbursements more traceable. More than 350 projects across 96 countries are already onboarded to its digital ledgers, letting everyone involved in a project see how money is being spent.
The stablecoin exploration would focus initially on an intermediated, interoperable model, limited to borrower countries where digital assets are permitted, with plans to involve other banks over time.
Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire framed development finance as one of the most important applications for his company’s technology, saying money that moves “at the speed of the internet shouldn’t be reserved for the world’s biggest banks and corporations.”
Today, the @WorldBankGroup announced work with @circle and @Citi to bring the benefits of USDC to global funds distribution. A big step towards a more efficient and inclusive financial system.https://t.co/hq436tA5IR
— Jeremy Allaire (@jerallaire) November 17, 2026
Citi’s Shahmir Khaliq said the collaboration would deliver “24/7 capabilities at scale so that critical funds move in real time.”
The move hands the stablecoin industry a powerful institutional validator, and it fits a broader wave of traditional finance embracing the technology.
Wall Street is currently racing to claim the onchain dollar, with Goldman Sachs, Citi and other banks committing roughly $270 million to a joint stablecoin venture, while Deutsche Bank recently went live with crypto custody after a five-year buildout.
For Circle, whose USDC is the second-largest stablecoin, a role in the World Bank’s payment plumbing marks a notable step toward mainstream legitimacy, even as the broader crypto market endures a rough stretch of ETF outflows and falling prices.

items.content:
In brief
- Bitcoin’s realized losses relative to past-year profits hit levels seen only near past cycle lows, Glassnode said, while leverage was largely flushed out.
- Buyers absorbed about 66,000 BTC between $62,000 and $66,000, but demand remains thin, with ETF outflows reaching about $2.2 billion in November.
- A daily close below $62,000 could send Bitcoin toward $58,500 or $53,700, while reclaiming $74,100 would confirm a bottom is forming, according to Glassnode.
Bitcoin’s latest crash has pushed investors into the kind of loss-taking that has historically shown up near market bottoms.
Realized losses, which investors lock in when they sell coins for less than they paid, have climbed relative to the profits taken over the past year.
That measure now sits at levels seen only near the lows of 2018, 2020, 2022 and early 2023, according to a report published Tuesday by onchain analytics firm Glassnode. It’s the first such reading since then.
BTC price on November 22, 4:59PM UTC
Most of the selling came from recent buyers. Holders of coins less than six months old took losses into early 2026, cashed in gains during the rally into September and October, and are now selling at a loss again, Glassnode said. Leverage has been flushed too, with Nov. 13 and 14 bringing some of the largest long liquidations relative to open interest since 2023.
Bitcoin fell to about $62,000 on Nov. 15 before bouncing, and it traded near $64,970 on Tuesday. More than $2 billion in liquidations over the weekend left traders watching $60,000 as a potential next stop, Decrypt reported. The slide deepened last week as fears of further Federal Reserve rate hikes erased Bitcoin’s summer rally. Rising interest rates generally do not bode well for risk assets like Bitcoin, since investors typically rotate to safer bets like U.S. Treasuries when rates elevate.
But there are early signs of support, according to Glassnode. Buyers absorbed about 66,000 BTC in the $62,000 to $66,000 range during the two days of heaviest selling, adding to a zone where recent buyers accumulated around the August low.
Resting bids on Binance and Coinbase within 5% of the price now outweigh asks by about 2.3 to 1. The Coinbase Premium, which compares Bitcoin’s price on Coinbase with global markets, briefly turned positive at the low as U.S. buyers stepped in.
Still, Glassnode stopped short of calling a bottom. Broad demand remains thin: stablecoin supply has shrunk 4.2% over 90 days, and the Coinbase Premium has slipped back to a small discount.
Meanwhile, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs extended their outflow streak to eight sessions on Monday and have bled about $2.2 billion so far in November, according to Decrypt’s ETF tracker.
That makes the $62,000 to $66,000 range the line to watch. Short-term holders bought very few coins below $62,000, and a large cluster of leveraged long positions sits just beneath it, between about $59,500 and $62,200.
A daily close below $62,000 could trigger a fast drop toward the June low of $58,500 and Bitcoin’s realized price of $53,700, the average price at which every coin last moved, Glassnode said.
On the upside, a move back above $74,100, the average cost basis of short-term holders, would confirm that a bottom is forming, according to the firm. Options traders on Deribit, meanwhile, price roughly a one-in-three chance that Bitcoin settles below $53,700 at the September 2027 expiry.
The Fed’s next rate decision is Dec. 9, a day before November inflation data is released.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Nate Kostar
items.content:
Eastern Europe crypto flows fall 7.9% as Ukraine draws $12B in stablecoins
Chainalysis found that Eastern Europe recorded the steepest decline in crypto activity of any region, while cross-border stablecoin transfers to Ukraine continued amid the ongoing war.
Eastern Europe recorded the steepest decline in cryptocurrency activity among the regions tracked by Chainalysis in the year ended June 2026, falling 7.9% even as retail-sized transfers increased in value, according to a report published Tuesday.
The region’s crypto economy shrank to $642.1 billion from $697.1 billion a year earlier, compared with a 1.6% decline globally, the report states. Russia, which accounted for roughly 44% of the regional total, saw activity fall 14.7% to $284.1 billion over the period. By contrast, Belarus recorded 27.6% growth, while Bulgaria, Moldova and Ukraine saw smaller increases.
The value of transfers of $10,000 or more to crypto services fell 17.4%, from $591.5 billion to $488.6 billion, according to the report.
The value of smaller transfers to crypto services, meanwhile, rose 8.3%. These retail-sized transfers accounted for 13.1% of the value sent to crypto services in Eastern Europe, the highest share of any region studied and above the global average of 10.1%.
Eastern European crypto activity by country, July 2025 to June 2026. Source: Chainalysis report
Polish crypto ATM activity grows
Crypto ATM activity also increased across Eastern Europe, with transaction volumes nearly doubling from $17.3 million to $33.9 million. Poland recorded a 120% increase in ATM transactions despite a 5% decline in centralized exchange activity, with stablecoins accounting for roughly 90% of its ATM transactions.
Chainalysis measures the crypto economy using inflows to crypto services, domestic transfers between personal wallets and cross-border inflows to personal wallets. The figures are measured in dollars, so cryptocurrency price changes can also affect the totals, according to its methodology.
Related: OpenPayd secures MiCA license as stablecoin adoption grows in Europe
Ukraine receives billions in stablecoins
Despite the broader regional decline, Ukraine remained a major destination for stablecoins, receiving $12 billion in cross-border wallet-to-wallet transfers. Of that, $2.41 billion was in retail-sized transfers below $10,000, according to Chainalysis.
Chainalysis also found that countries with larger Ukrainian populations, including prewar diaspora communities and refugees who arrived after Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022, generally sent more stablecoins to Ukraine. Among the 36 countries studied across Europe and North America,
Canada was the largest source of retail-sized, remittance-like transfers, at $359 million.
Crypto transfers to Ukraine by diaspora population, July 2025 to June 2026. Source: Chainalysis report
A Chainalysis spokesperson told Cointelegraph that the cross-border flows were largely denominated in US dollar-pegged stablecoins, although the firm did not provide a breakdown by individual token.

items.author: Oluwapelumi Adejumo
items.content:
Quick Take
- A Bitcoin developer verified a 9.39 GB snapshot containing 164.5 million unspent transaction outputs in just 72 seconds.
- The experimental system could significantly reduce Bitcoin node setup times by replacing extensive historical checks with compact cryptographic proofs.
- The developer now wants to integrate the technology into Bitcoin Core, but incomplete validation checks and security requirements remain obstacles.
A Bitcoin developer has shown how to verify a 9.39 GB blockchain snapshot in just 72 seconds, potentially making it easier and faster to run Bitcoin nodes.
The developer, identified as l-henri, disclosed the experiment in a Nov. 13 Delving Bitcoin post, describing a system that uses cryptographic proofs to check Bitcoin's existing transaction records without independently processing its entire history.
The experiment involved a snapshot containing approximately 164.5 million unspent transaction outputs (UTXOs) at Bitcoin block 972,500. These outputs represent Bitcoin that has been received but not yet spent, forming the database nodes use to determine whether coins remain available for transactions.
Using an arm64 computer with approximately 0.5 GB of memory, the developer checked that the snapshot matched the records established by a cryptographic proof.
The process took approximately 72 seconds, with nearly all that time spent reading the 9.39 GB file. Separately, the developer demonstrated that a compact 1.6 MB proof could be verified in a web browser in about half a second.
The achievement could help address a practical challenge of running Bitcoin infrastructure: the time and computing resources required to verify historical blockchain activity before a node becomes fully operational.
How cryptographic proofs could speed up Bitcoin node setup
Bitcoin nodes help secure the network by independently checking transactions and enforcing its rules.
Traditionally, setting up a fully validating node involves downloading and processing BTC's historical transactions to reconstruct the current database of spendable coins.
Bitcoin Core already offers a shortcut through a feature called assumeUTXO, which lets nodes start operating using a snapshot of the blockchain's transaction state. However, the software continues verifying historical transactions in the background to confirm that the snapshot accurately reflects Bitcoin's records.
L-henri's experiment proposes replacing that additional verification work with a cryptographic proof. This approach could let new nodes accept a verified snapshot without repeating extensive historical calculations, potentially reducing setup time and resource requirements.
The developer's system uses STARK proofs, which allow computers to verify specified calculations without repeating every step themselves. In this experiment, the proof covered BTC's block headers from its beginning and checked changes to unspent coins between blocks 935,001 and 972,500.
However, the calculations started from an existing trusted Bitcoin Core snapshot at block 935,000 rather than rebuilding the entire transaction history. The system also excluded checks of transaction scripts and signatures, meaning it does not yet provide the same verification guarantees as a fully validating BTC node.
These limitations remain important as the developer considers integrating the technology into Bitcoin Core.
In the November disclosure, l-henri proposed testing a modification that would let Bitcoin Core accept proof-backed snapshots and skip its existing background validation process.
That would mark a departure from Bitcoin Core's current approach, which independently checks historical records even after loading a snapshot.
The project remains experimental and has not undergone an external security review. Bitcoin Core also does not currently support the proposed integration.
The next step is to test whether the proof system can provide sufficient verification guarantees to replace historical checks without weakening the security assumptions BTC nodes rely on.
